elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "Corio, as the Customer under this Agreement, may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Commerce One". The element is satisfied in the disjunctive by an Agreement-level convenience right; no Order Form structure exists in this contract.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Commerce One" — exactly 30 days, written, and no additional conditions or Vendor consent are attached.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "Commerce One shall refund to Corio, on a pro-rata basis, any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination." Pro-rata is expressly stated, not merely inferred from the post-termination period.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Retained § 11.2 confines termination to uncured material breach and insolvency; § 11.1's 30-day notice is a non-renewal mechanic expressly keyed to "prior to the expiration of the initial five (5) year term or any one (1) year renewal", i.e. effective at term end and evaluated under RENEWAL. No mid-term Vendor convenience exit exists.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted right runs on thirty (30) days' notice, which is outside the 60-90 day fallback band (and better for Customer). Not a defect given the preferred level is complete.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Conditional element whose condition does not apply: no early-termination charge, acceleration or contingent payment mechanic appears in § 11 or Exhibit B, so there is no fee to cap.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: § 11.2 gives Commerce One only breach/insolvency termination; the sole notice-based exit in § 11.1 takes effect at expiration of the then-current initial or renewal term, so any Vendor convenience exit is term-end-only.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: § 11.1 requires only "at least thirty (30) days prior to the expiration" notice from either party; no 90-day Vendor notice was added. Irrelevant to completion because the preferred level is satisfied.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all four preferred elements are met — the new clause supplies the Customer convenience right, the 30-day written notice and an express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and retained § 11.2 already denies Commerce One any mid-term convenience exit.
The 'deviation' status is correct: before the edit a five-year committed term offered Corio no convenience exit at all, which is walk-away territory under this rule.

Minimality holds: a single concise insertion for a missing clause, no deletion or paraphrase of existing § 11.1/§ 11.2 language, no survival tail, no at-own-expense or procedural extras, and the model language's surplus 'in whole or in part' was correctly dropped since there is no Order Form or partial-termination structure.

Intent preserved: breach, insolvency, warranty-condition and auto-renewal mechanics survive verbatim; no undefined terms or dangling cross-references are introduced. The identifier 'Corio, as the Customer under this Agreement' is descriptive and does not create a new defined term.

The deterministic check 'Customer convenience termination present: false' is a false negative on inspection — the rendered text plainly contains a Customer-side convenience termination ('Corio, as the Customer ... may terminate this Agreement for convenience'); the regex appears to match only a literal 'Customer may terminate' string. No drafting repair is required on that account.
Optional polish only (not a defect): the insertion is untitled/unnumbered in the rendered output; giving it a section number such as § 11.2A would avoid any citation ambiguity within Article 11.
